speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the nature of your neck and arm pain, and specify which fingers are experiencing the numbness or tingling?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain and numbness radiate down a specific arm in a dermatomal pattern, or is it symmetric in both hands? I also need to know if you have experienced any loss of bowel or bladder control or difficulty walking.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of fasciculations, absent reflexes, and weakness in both hands alongside sensory symptoms is concerning for lower motor neuron involvement. I need to rule out structural causes like cervical myelopathy or radiculopathy, so I will order imaging and nerve conduction studies. REQUEST TEST: Cervical MRI, Nerve Conduction Studies, EMG.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The MRI confirms a syrinx, and your symptoms of dissociated sensory loss—specifically the loss of pain and temperature sensation with preserved vibration and proprioception—are classic for this condition. This presentation is known as a "cape-like" distribution of sensory loss.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Syringomyelia
